title: Orchestration catalog for team handoffs and fallback scenarios
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create an orchestration catalog (living registry + decision matrix) that standardizes how teams handshake ownership for launch windows and the automated/manual fallback scenarios if a dependency misses its SLA. The catalog will be used by PMs, ENG leads, Design, Security, and Infra to: 1) declare hard vs. soft dependencies, 2) assign cutover owners and backups, 3) define measurable risk thresholds tied to observable signals, and 4) publish a clear roll-forward/roll-back procedure. Goal: reduce ad-hoc escalations during multi-squad launches and provide a machine-readable registry for the Roadmap Orchestrator to introspect during cutover gating.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog schema published in Confluence with field-level definitions (dependency_type, owner, backup_owner, impact_window, SLO_signal, fallback_action, rollback_criteria)
ESLint-style JSON schema for machine-readable registry checked into infra-config (repo link in links)
Three representative launch lanes (Hosted API feature, Dedicated autoscaling change, Private deploy upgrade) documented end-to-end with owners and fallback scripts
Runbook includes stakeholder contact matrix, escalation path, and playbook checklist validated in a cross-team dry run
Automated gating rule prototype that flags 'high risk' launches when two or more hard dependencies are in red less than 72 hours before cutover
deliverables: JSON schema and sample registry entries in infra-config repo
Cutover playbook template (PDF/Confluence) and a worked example for a Q2 feature
Dry-run report with action items and owner sign-offs
Proposal for integrating gating signals into Roadmap Orchestrator
milestones: 2026-02-28: Schema proposal and initial stakeholder review
2026-04-01: Final playbook and Confluence page published
2026-04-15: Handshake process adopted for next quarter planning cycle
risks: Teams may under-specify backups leading to leftover manual work
SLO signals required for gating may not exist for older services
Security review for automated fallback actions could delay rollout
False positives from gating rules could block low-risk launches if thresholds are too strict
